title: Welcome to the Ballroom
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Aimless middle schooler Tatara Fujita is rescued from bullies by Kaname Sengoku, a champion Latin dancer, and stumbles into competitive ballroom dancesport. Inspired by classmate Shizuku Hanaoka, he trains, partners with the strong-willed Chinatsu Hiyama and measures himself against rivals such as Kiyoharu Hyodo and Masami Kugimiya.
life_message: A good life is found by committing wholly to a craft and learning to move in step with a partner.

content.note: Tatara is bullied and extorted; Sengoku intimidates the delinquents (Wikipedia, AniList).
Teen crush on Shizuku; close-contact dance and some comic suggestive moments (to verify); MangaDex safe.
Rough teasing and shouting from mentors and rivals (to verify).
Tatara's aimlessness and low self-worth; Masami's hidden insecurity (Wikipedia).

dominant: Mastery through discipline; self-discovery through art; partnership

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Rivalries with Kiyoharu and Masami turn on pride, but disputes are settled on the competition floor.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Strict studio training, coaches and competition rules shape Tatara's growth.

Civic vs kin.evidence: The dance studio community, not family, supports Tatara.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Coaches and champions like Sengoku and Marisa command deference; lead-follow roles are debated.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: A tradition-bound Western art form pursued with modern, secular ambition.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Dance is above all Tatara finding and expressing himself.

folkways.japan: Strict senpai-kohai and coach-student hierarchy in the studio reflects Japanese training culture in arts and sports.

delivery.evidence: Coming-of-age dance story (AniList Dancing, Coming of Age); no source comments on delivery (to verify)
delivery.note: Commitment to a craft and partnership are shown through training and competition.

winners_losers: Tatara gains purpose, skill and partners; bullies and passivity lose. Sympathy goes to dedication and genuine partnership.
